manifest.name: Restaurant
manifest.summary: Restaurant extensions for the Point of Sale

behavioral_notes.observation: A restaurant.floor (name, background_color/image, sequence) is linked many2many to the restaurant-enabled pos.config(s) and owns a one2many of restaurant.table records. Each table carries pixel-geometry fields (position_h, position_v, width, height, shape square/round, color, seats) that exist purely to render the draggable floor-plan in the OWL app -- these are not accounting data. On creating/enabling a restaurant config, pos.config._setup_default_floor auto-creates one floor named after the company plus one default table, so a till is never floor-less. floor.write and table @api.ondelete guards block editing/removing a floor or table while a non-closed pos.session uses its config, and floor.deactivate_floor / table.are_orders_still_in_draft refuse to remove anything that still has draft (open) orders, protecting in-progress dining.

The extension adds table_id (Many2one restaurant.table) and customer_count (Guests) to pos.order, binding a sit-down order to its physical table. _get_open_order is overridden so that, only when config.module_pos_restaurant is true, re-opening a table resolves to the existing draft order by uuid OR by (table_id + state='draft' + config_id) -- i.e. tapping an occupied table reloads its running tab rather than starting a new ticket. This table-keyed open-order lookup (and the draft-tab semantics) lives entirely in Python and the OWL client and is invisible to metadata.

restaurant.order.course models a meal 'course' (e.g. starters, mains): index for ordering, a uuid, order_id->pos.order and line_ids->pos.order.line, plus a fired Boolean. pos.order.line gains course_id (ondelete='set null') so each ordered item is grouped into a course. On both create and write, when fired is set true the model stamps fired_date = now() server-side -- the timestamp of when the kitchen was told to start that course (firing). pos.session._set_last_order_preparation_change snapshots line state (qty, product, attributes, note) into the order's last_order_preparation_change JSON, the basis for computing what to send to the kitchen/bar preparation printer. None of this coursing/firing/prep-diff logic is derivable from field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: pos.config restaurant feature flags (iface_splitbill / iface_printbill / set_tip_after_payment / default_screen)
behavioral_notes.observation: pos.config is extended with Booleans iface_splitbill (enable bill splitting), iface_printbill (print a proforma bill before payment; defaulted True for restaurant configs at create), set_tip_after_payment (let card terminals adjust the authorized amount to add a tip after the guest leaves), and default_screen (tables|register). create/write also force show_product_images/show_category_images defaults and gate set_tip_after_payment on iface_tipproduct; floor_ids is added to _get_forbidden_change_fields so floors can't be silently swapped on a live config. These flags switch on the SplitBillScreen, the pre-payment bill print, post-payment tip adjustment and whether the app opens on the floor plan -- behaviors that are pure config-driven UI branches.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (restaurant extension of the offline OWL POS app) -- table transfer, split bill, coursing, tips
behavioral_notes.observation: pos_restaurant is delivered almost entirely as JS/OWL bolted onto the standalone offline point_of_sale terminal app (it injects into the point_of_sale._assets_pos bundle, not a separate SPA). It adds 7 OWL components / ~31 JS files / 21 XML templates and registers 3 new pos_pages screens -- FloorScreen (drag-and-drop floor plan built on a makeDraggableHook/useDraggable; tables are repositioned and table-merge is detected via on-screen rectangle intersection), SplitBillScreen (split one order's lines into separate orders/bills), and TipScreen (collect/adjust tips, incl. set-tip-after-payment) -- plus an OrderCourse component for coursing and ~25 prototype patches onto base POS screens/models (ProductScreen, ControlButtons, ActionpadWidget, TicketScreen, OrderSummary, PaymentScreen lines, PosStore/PosOrder/PosOrderline) that add restaurant control buttons, table transfer between tables, guest count, course actions and proforma-bill printing. Transfer-between-tables and split-bill happen client-side against the POS's IndexedDB-backed offline ORM and only later sync to pos.order on the server; this entire interaction model is reverse-engineerable only from the static JS, never from Python metadata.

it_architecture.application: pos_restaurant (Restaurant extension of the Point of Sale application component: adds floor/table/course backend models + restaurant screens to the offline OWL POS terminal app)
software_services: (no own HTTP/JSON-RPC routes; extends point_of_sale's /pos/ui terminal app and pos.session data-loading + sync_from_ui RPCs)
information_flows: config gate: restaurant models (restaurant.floor/table/order.course) are loaded into the terminal only when pos.config.module_pos_restaurant is true (pos.session._load_pos_data_models)
side-effect: pos.config._setup_default_floor -> auto-create one restaurant.floor + one restaurant.table when a restaurant/bar config is created or enabled
side-effect: restaurant.order.course.create/write with fired=True -> stamp fired_date=now() (kitchen firing time)
frontend path: FloorScreen/SplitBillScreen mutate table assignment and split orders in the offline OWL/IndexedDB client, then replay to pos.order via point_of_sale's sync_from_ui
downstream (inherited from point_of_sale): the finished pos.order still drives stock.picking + account.move at payment/session close

capabilities: Manage Restaurant Floors & Table Layout (floor plan)
Assign Orders to Tables & Track Guest Count
value_streams: Dine-in service: seat guests at table -> open table order (table_id + guest count) -> order by course / fire to kitchen -> print proforma bill -> split bill if needed -> tender payment + tip -> (inherited) deliver stock + close session journal entry
organization: point_of_sale.group_pos_user (read floors/tables; full CRUD on courses)
policies: no own ir.rule (0 record rules); 5 ir.model.access rows reuse the inherited group_pos_user / group_pos_manager groups
floors/tables read-only for pos_user, manager-only create/write/unlink; restaurant.order.course writable by pos_user (the cashier edits coursing live)
cannot delete/deactivate a floor or table while a non-closed pos.session uses its config (@api.ondelete + write guards)
cannot delete a floor/table that still has draft orders (deactivate_floor / are_orders_still_in_draft)
stakeholders: Kitchen / Bar staff (consume course firing & preparation changes)
metrics: customer_count (guests served per order) -- inferred, no dedicated report model in this module
course fired_date timestamps (kitchen firing timing) -- inferred

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: pos_restaurant is a thin sell-side extension of point_of_sale, which is itself a value-chain primary activity (the originating act is the in-restaurant sale/checkout that produces a paid pos.order and drives downstream delivery (stock.picking) and revenue/cash recognition (account.move at session close)). It therefore inherits value_model 'chain' / activity_class 'primary' and maps to APQC 3.0 (Market and Sell) -- the dine-in order is the 3.5 'manage sales orders' family realized as a table-served till; deliver (APQC 4.0) and AR/cash (APQC 9.0) remain triggered side-effects, not this module's mission. The module's own added value is service-orchestration (floor plan, table assignment, coursing/firing, bill splitting, tips), giving it a pronounced 'shop' (service-encounter / dining experience) overtone, and -- like its parent -- a strong network/frontend character: nearly all of its logic ships as OWL screens patched into the offline IndexedDB-backed POS terminal app, with no server HTTP routes of its own.

standard_capabilities: graphical floor plan with draggable, resizable tables (shape/seats/color) across multiple floors
table-bound orders with guest (customer) count and reload-the-tab-by-table behavior
course management and kitchen/bar firing with preparation-change tracking
bill splitting (SplitBillScreen) and pre-payment proforma bill printing
tips, including adjust-tip-after-payment via card terminals
auto-provisioned default floor + table when a restaurant/bar config is enabled
onboarding 'Restaurant' and 'Bar' scenarios with demo floors, categories and presets
typical_fits: sit-down restaurant / bar counter service with table-served checks
split-the-check and pay-with-tip at the table
coursed service firing to kitchen/bar printers
single restaurant config toggled on via module_pos_restaurant on pos.config
common_gaps: reservation / waitlist management (not in scope here)
complex kitchen display systems beyond the basic preparation-change/printer flow
advanced floor-plan constraints (capacity optimization, table combination rules) beyond simple parent_id grouping
custom split logic (per-seat allocation, item-share splitting) beyond the standard SplitBillScreen
deep coursing automation (timed auto-fire, pacing) -- firing is manual
any new offline/client screen or table-state behavior requires OWL development, not configuration
drive_hints: browse /pos/ui/<config_id> on a restaurant config to launch the floor-plan FloorScreen

open_questions: Exact split-bill algorithm in SplitBillScreen (per-line vs per-quantity vs per-seat) and how it materializes new pos.order records on sync.
Full transfer/merge-between-tables flow: how parent_id grouping and table_id reassignment are persisted and conflict-resolved across two devices offline.
How course firing drives the actual kitchen/bar preparation printout (preparation-change diff -> printer) -- the print path lives in the parent module / hardware proxy.
Precise post-payment tip adjustment mechanics with external payment terminals (set_tip_after_payment) and which payment add-on modules support it.
